descriptionChirho: To undergo a change of state or condition, transitioning from one quality or status to another; the core transformative meaning of ginomai (Arabic: صَارَ sara; Korean: 되다 doeda; Swahili: -kuwa).
To take place as an event or incident, denoting that something occurred, came to pass, or will come to pass (Arabic: حَدَثَ hadatha; Korean: 일어나다 ireonada; Swahili: -tokea).
To come into a place or situation, denoting physical or temporal arrival rather than transformation or event occurrence (Arabic: جَاءَ ja'a / وَصَلَ wasala; Korean: 오다 oda; Swahili: -kuja/-fika).

To exist, be present, or find oneself in a state or location, denoting simple existence or being without implying transformation (Arabic: كَانَ kana / كَائِنًا ka'inan; Korean: 있다 itda; Swahili: -kuwa in stative sense).

labelChirho: let it be, may it be done
descriptionChirho: Jussive or imperatival wish expressing a command or prayer for something to come into being or be accomplished (Arabic: لِيَكُنْ li-yakun / لِيَصِرْ li-yasir; Korean: 되라 doera / 이루어지소서; Swahili: na iwe).

Idiomatic strong negative optative expressing emphatic denial or abhorrence at a proposition, a Pauline formula of absolute rejection (Arabic: حَاشَا hasha; Korean: 그럴 수 없다 geureol su eopda; Swahili: hasha!).

To be created, manufactured, or brought about by an external agent, emphasizing the passive result of making or doing (Arabic: صُنِعَ suni'a / تَمَّ tamma / تُصْنَعُ tusna'u; Korean: 만들어지다 mandeurejida / 이루어지다 iruejida; Swahili: -fanywa/-tengenezwa).
To come into being through birth or origination, emphasizing the beginning of personal existence rather than state change (Arabic: مَولودًا mawludan; Korean: 나다 nada; Swahili: -zaliwa).
